items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: a friend of mine who I'd known through school up in Oakland, by the name of Charlie Eckels, had an orchestra that worked over here in Los Angeles... I was still going -- trying to go to school... from then on I was a professional musician.

ctx.x: He couldn't stand that in any form. So I moved out to my cousin's house up in North Pasadena, and I was still going -- trying to go to school, which I did for a while, but finally had to quit, and from then on I was a professional musician.

I think I was out of work for about two weeks, when a friend of mine who I'd known through school up in Oakland, by the name of Charlie Eckels, had an orchestra that worked over here in Los Angeles in a place called 401 Ballroom, which was one of the establishments where they usually call these places dime-a-dance parlors.
And that was in Los Angeles?
